conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I’m Dr. Lee. I understand you came in because of a fever?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I felt achy around noon, checked my temp, it was 99.3. By 4 PM it was 100.6 with chills. My hepatologist told me to come in.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Got it. You’ve been on ertapenem for cholangitis, right? Any signs of infection in the PICC line?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No pain or redness in the arm. I’ve had 21 PICCs—my PICCs are old enough to drink now!

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s dedication. We’ll run blood and urine cultures. You’re scheduled for transplant soon—this might be a pre-op admission.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I hope so. I’ve been on a liquid diet today—loose stools, but no fever since 4 PM.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll monitor that. Your ultrasound shows cirrhosis and gallstones, but no biliary dilation. We’ll keep you on antibiotics just in case.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good news—your cultures were negative. You’re going to surgery today for your living donor liver transplant.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m ready. Any concerns?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The team will monitor blood flow during surgery. We’ll see you after.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The transplant went technically well, but after surgery, we noticed no blood flow in the portal vein on ultrasound.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that bad?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It is. You were taken back to the OR. They opened the abdomen due to compartment syndrome and placed a wound VAC.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We found the portal vein flow was reversed—going the wrong way. This is likely due to a ‘steal’ from varices. You had a procedure to fix it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What did they do?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: They placed a stent in the portal vein and embolized some varices to redirect blood flow into the liver. A liver biopsy showed ischemic changes, not rejection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So it’s not rejection?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not yet. We’re giving you Thymoglobulin to prevent immune reaction. Your liver enzymes are improving.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The good news is, the portal flow is now going the right way—hepatopetal. The VAC is helping your wound.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s a relief. When can I breathe on my own?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re still intubated, but we closed your abdomen yesterday. Today, we’re placing a feeding tube because you’re malnourished.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: It didn’t go into my small intestine?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not yet—it looped in your stomach. We’ll try again later. For now, we’ll start continuous feeds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You had a seizure-like episode. EEG shows encephalopathy, not a seizure. CT and MRI ruled out stroke or PRES.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I feel foggy. Is that why?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. We started Keppra just in case. Your mental status should improve.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We found a clot in a branch of your right hepatic vein. It’s not blocking major flow, but we’re watching it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Another clot? What caused it?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Likely from the surgery and altered blood flow. We’re on a heparin drip to prevent it from growing.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your labs show rising bilirubin and WBC. We’re concerned about cholangitis. Starting vancomycin and meropenem.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: But my stool test was negative for C. diff.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: This is likely biliary cholangitis, not C. diff. We’ll treat it aggressively.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The ultrasound shows some flow returning to the hepatic vein. That’s a good sign.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my pain?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We think it’s from a small area of liver necrosis. We’ll keep you on oxycodone for comfort.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your drain output is high—600–800 cc/day. We’re giving albumin and watching your blood counts.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I feel weak.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your hemoglobin dropped. We gave two units of blood. It’s stable now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We did a cholangiogram—no leaks or blockages. That’s excellent.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So the bile ducts are okay?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. The T-tube is working well. We’ll keep monitoring.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re doing a liver biopsy today to check for rejection or cholestasis.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is it safe?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, ultrasound-guided. Minimal risk. We need to rule out rejection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Biopsy showed biliary ischemia, not rejection. We’re continuing antibiotics.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No rejection? That’s good, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Very good. Your liver is healing from the vascular issues.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve had rising WBC and confusion. CT shows a new area of poor blood flow in the liver—segment V/VI.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is it getting worse?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s a sign of ongoing vascular compromise, but no infection. We’re doing another biopsy and vein dilation.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We dilated the hepatic vein and took a transjugular biopsy. The vein stenosis improved.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the biopsy?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No rejection. Just ischemic changes. We’ll keep you on antibiotics for two more weeks.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your labs are improving—bilirubin down to 1.5, WBC normal. You’re starting to eat and walk with a walker.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I feel stronger. When can I go home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not yet. You’ll go to rehab first. You still need wound care and monitoring.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your TSH is high—15. We’re increasing your levothyroxine to 100 mcg.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been tired—could that be why?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. That should help your energy. We also started fludrocortisone for potassium issues.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing great. Rehab approved you. Discharge is tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What meds will I be on?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Tacrolimus, mycophenolate, prednisone, warfarin, insulin, and antibiotics for four more days. Plus your thyroid and stomach meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the PICC line?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, for IV meds. You’ll have home nursing. Call us if you have fever, pain, or bleeding.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you for everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re ready. The VAC stays on until the wound heals. Keep the Broviac capped. Follow up with the transplant clinic.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll be careful. I’m just glad to be moving forward.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: So are we. You’ve been through a lot. Keep up the good work.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care. We’ll see you in clinic soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll be there.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: One more thing—check your blood sugar and BP daily. Report any high values.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. I’ll keep a log.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. And don’t stop any meds without calling us—especially with transplant drugs.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I won’t. I know how important they are.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Great. You’re all set for discharge.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Doctor.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Let the nurse know when you’re ready to leave.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thanks again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing great. Keep it up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Have a safe trip to rehab.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I’m ready for the next step.
